notes:
Both target workbooks (Rescheduled.xlsx and Restructured_Feb'21.xlsx) are "full history" workbooks: each replays the ENTIRE loan life from the 2015-02-24 drawdown through its own final maturity, rather than showing only the delta. Rows 1-41 (2015-03-15 through 2019-06-16) are byte-identical to the ORIGINAL EX_DATA['GHEL'] schedule in both files, confirming both descend from the same original. Two distinct events were identified, and — per instructions — both are modeled as new versions starting from the SAME effective date/opening balance (2019-12-15, opening 12,437,514.13) since the Restructured file supersedes/replaces the Rescheduled file's plan for all dates from 2020-03-15 onward (this is IDCOL's normal pattern: a later, more comprehensive restructuring workbook obsoletes an earlier reschedule workbook rather than building on its output).

1) RESCHEDULE ("1st Rescheduling", found in GHEL_Loan sheet label): at 2019-09-15 an overdue amount of 5,900,412.99 (unpaid principal/interest arrears bundled together) was rolled into the closing balance (jumping from a "clean" 6,537,101.14 to 12,437,514.13, cross-checked against the true original-schedule closing balance for that date). At 2019-12-15, interest of 188,635.63 accrued on the new balance and was fully capitalized (0 principal paid), landing at opening balance 12,626,149.76 for the resumed amortization. From 2020-03-15 the loan re-amortizes over 29 more quarterly installments (principal payments INCREASE each period: 350,739 -> 532,149) ending exactly at zero on 2027-03-15. This principal-increasing profile could not be reproduced by a simple annuity or flat-level-principal formula from first principles (verified: opening/29 flat-level-principal does not match the actual figures), so override arrays (interest_payment_amounts/opening_balance_amounts/closing_balance_amounts) pin every row to the workbook's exact numbers. Total capitalized amount per the workbook's own "Total Capitalized Amount (1st Rescheduling)" label is 388,345.42 (this is the sum of interest capitalized across Jun'19 partial / Sep'19 / Dec'19 rows — a subset of the overdue roll-in described above, i.e. these overlap rather than stack; overdueAmountRolledIn captures the full balance jump, capitalizedAmount reflects the workbook's own labeled interest-capitalization subtotal).

2) RESTRUCTURE ("DFIM Restructuring", also found in GHEL_Loan sheet with rows labeled "Mar'20 Interest Due/Payment/Partial Capitalization", "Jun'20/Sep'20/Dec'20 Capitalization", "Total DFIM Capitalization" = 644,514.82): this event starts from the IDENTICAL 2019-12-15 balance as the Rescheduled version (12,626,149.76 opening for Mar'20) but imposes a full moratorium — zero principal AND the interest itself is capitalized (added to balance) for four quarters (Mar'20 through Dec'20), consistent with Bangladesh Bank/DFIM COVID-era deferment circulars (label says "DFIM Restructuring" but no specific circular number is given in the workbook, so regulatoryReference is a paraphrase, not a verbatim citation — treat with some caution). Principal resumes 2021-03-15 and the principal-payment stream for 2021-03-15 onward is IDENTICAL, value-for-value, to the Rescheduled version's stream just shifted by exactly 4 quarters (verified 372,261.63 / 377,845.56 / 383,513.24 / 389,265.94 / 395,104.93 match exactly) — confirming the restructure reused the reschedule's already-computed principal ladder and simply delayed it, appending 4 extra tail installments (519,838.59 each) at a reduced flat amount to absorb the additional capitalized interest, ending exactly at zero on 2028-03-15. Because this principal stream is inherited from another workbook (not derivable from the restructure's own first principles) and involves a moratorium with quarterly interest capitalization, the full override-array approach was used here as well.

Interest rate remained 6% (unchanged) through both events — day-count basis 360 confirmed exactly via recomputation (opening*0.06*days/360 reproduces the workbook interest to the cent for both non-capitalizing and capitalizing periods). waivedAmount is 0 for both — no forgiveness found; all irregular amounts are capitalization (added to principal) or overdue-rollup, never write-off. overdueAmountRolledIn (5,900,412.99) is reported identically for both versions since both share the same 2019-09-15 rollup event as their common ancestor point; it is NOT double-counted across the two facility versions in aggregate borrower exposure — they are alternate/successive plans for the same debt, not two additive facilities.

Tenor figures: tenorMonthsBefore/After are measured in total months from the original financial_close (2015-01-31) to each version's final maturity, since "before" tenor for the very first event is the original 8-year (96-month) sanctioned tenor. RESCHEDULE extends total tenor to 146 months (final maturity 2027-03-15); RESTRUCTURE further extends it to 158 months (final maturity 2028-03-15). tenorMonthsBefore for the RESTRUCTURE event is set to the RESCHEDULE's resulting 146 months (its immediate "before" state) even though, per the note above, both events are modeled from the same 2019-12-15 branch point rather than the restructure literally building atop the reschedule's later data.

No separate co-financier tranche or additional facility was found for GHEL in these two files — one IDCOL facility, two successive version records.
